raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation After PR #24013 landed, Ascend NPU VLM serving (ViT CUDA/NPU graph + ascend_attn) regressed on high-concurrency 1080p workloads (e.g. Qwen3.6-27B performance cases that previously passed on TP2). Two separate issues showed up: 1. TND seqlen mismatch on the ViT NPU graph path npu_fused_infer_attention_score with input_layout="TND" requires actual_seq_lengths to be cumulative (same semantics as cu_seqlens[1:]), and the last element must equal query.shape[0]. ViTNpuGraphRunner still stored per-sequence lengths (cu_seqlens[1:] - cu_seqlens[:-1]), which matched the old _npu_flash_attention_unpad API but not TND. This often passed for a single image (last length == T by accident) and failed after #24013 packed many images into one ViT call (e.g. queryT=89760 vs last=8160). 2. Unbounded cross-request ViT batching OOM on NPU #24013 batches all per-image cache misses across requests into one ViT forward. HIP already falls back to the per-request path because large cross-request batches regressed on ROCm CI; NPU followed the CUDA batching path with no cap. On large images + high concurrency this spikes peak memory (even when LLM prefill batching of many seqs is fine). This risk was also raised in review (discussion) with a suggested VIT_ENCODE_MAX_TOKENS split, but that was not implemented for CUDA/NPU. ## Modifications vit_npu_graph_runner.py Cache cu_seqlens[1:] (cumulative) for graph capture instead of per-sequence deltas, so TND actual_seq_lengths matches queryT under multi-image ViT batches. mm_utils.py Treat NPU like HIP for per-image embedding: use _get_chunked_embedding_by_item (per-request ViT) instead of _batch_encode_per_image_misses (cross-request batch), via if _is_hip or _is_npu to avoid OOM when making vit call for too much images at once. ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling Ran two tests. 1. 2 image per request, for a total of 2 requests. 3. 1 Image per request, total of 42 requests on file test_npu_qwen3_6_35b_a3b_1p_in1080p_30_out256_50ms.py ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 4. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 5. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 6. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #29714110662](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29714110662) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #29714110681](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29714110681)
